festivals_events: Occasional local events; main draw is nature and activities.
unique_experiences: Boat rides on clear river where boats appear to float on air in good conditions, with camping options along riverbank.
activities_available: Kayaking, snorkelling and cliff jumping with operators
Short walks and suspension bridge views
best_seasons: Post-monsoon to winter when water is clearest (roughly November-February).
avoid_seasons: Peak monsoon when river can be muddy and water levels/flow risky.
Very crowded holiday weekends if seeking quiet.

road_connectivity: Road from Jowai with last stretch on narrower hilly roads; walks and steps from parking to falls.
atm_availability: ATMs in Jowai; not at falls.
internet_connectivity: Limited mobile signal around falls.
off_season: Monsoon and very rainy spells
rainfall_pattern: Heavy monsoon rainfall; water colour and flow vary by season.
food_scene: Small stalls and basic eateries near parking; carry snacks and water.
local_culture: Falls are in Jaintia region with local communities managing some facilities.
local_customs: Follow local rules, especially regarding swimwear and behaviour around families.
festivals_events: No major standalone festival; visited as scenic nature spot.
unique_experiences: Striking turquoise waterfall pool that looks almost unreal in sunlight, reached via a scenic trail and steps.
activities_available: Guided swimming in designated safe area (with life jackets where allowed).
accommodation_types: Stay in Jowai or Shillong and visit as day trip
Very limited basic stays near falls area
best_seasons: Post-monsoon and winter for clearer water and safe access.
avoid_seasons: Periods of very heavy rain or unsafe flow when access may be restricted.

road_connectivity: Good roads from Haridwar, Dehradun and Delhi; frequent buses and shared vehicles.
atm_availability: Many ATMs around main market and ghats.
internet_connectivity: Good 4G and Wi-Fi in most tourist areas.
off_season: Monsoon months for adventure; shoulder weeks see fewer crowds
rainfall_pattern: North Indian monsoon pattern with heavy July-August rains.
food_scene: Vegetarian-heavy with many cafes offering global health foods and traditional Indian meals.
local_culture: Spiritual pilgrimage town with mix of long-stay seekers and short-term tourists.
local_customs: Conservative dress recommended at ghats/ashrams; remove footwear at temples and some ashram areas.
festivals_events: Yoga festivals, Ganga-related religious festivals, and seasonal fairs.
unique_experiences: Yoga capital on the banks of the Ganga with both spiritual retreats and adventure rafting in one base.
avoid_seasons: Peak monsoon for rafting safety issues; hottest May afternoons for outdoor activities

road_connectivity: Excellent road links from Delhi and other North Indian cities; frequent buses and trains.
atm_availability: Many ATMs in town and near busy areas.
internet_connectivity: Good 4G across town.
peak_tourist_season: Festivals (Kumbh, Kanwar Yatra periods, major Hindu holidays) and winter months
off_season: Very hot months; some monsoon weeks
rainfall_pattern: North Indian monsoon; occasional flood advisories along ghats.
food_scene: Largely vegetarian with street snacks, sweets and North Indian meals.
local_culture: Deeply religious city with constant pilgrim footfall.
local_customs: Dress modestly, remove footwear before entering temples, and respect queuing systems and Aarti protocols.
festivals_events: Kumbh Mela (periodic), Kanwar Yatra, Diwali and other major Hindu festivals.
unique_experiences: Major Hindu pilgrimage city where the Ganga enters plains, with large daily Aarti and Kumbh Mela at intervals.
activities_available: Taking dips in Ganga at designated ghats
Shopping for religious items and sweets
avoid_seasons: Peak summer heat and extremely crowded festival days unless specifically targeting them

road_connectivity: Good highway and rail links from major North Indian cities; city traffic can be congested near old town.
atm_availability: Many ATMs throughout city.
internet_connectivity: Good 4G and broadband in most parts.
nearest_airport_name: Lal Bahadur Shastri International Airport, Varanasi
off_season: Peak summer and some monsoon periods
rainfall_pattern: Ganga water levels vary with monsoon; boat routes may change.
food_scene: Street food (chaat, kachori, lassi), mithai shops and sit-down restaurants offering North Indian and some international options.
local_culture: Core Hindu pilgrimage city with centuries-old traditions and scholarship.
local_customs: Dress modestly, remove footwear at temples and be mindful at cremation ghats.
festivals_events: Dev Deepawali, Diwali, Holi, Ganga Mahotsav and more.
unique_experiences: One of the world's oldest living cities with intense spiritual rituals along Ganga ghats and maze-like old lanes.
avoid_seasons: Hottest months (May-June) and times of extreme flood or festival crowds if you dislike crowds

road_connectivity: Well-connected by highways and trains from Delhi, Chandigarh and other Punjab cities.
atm_availability: ATMs widespread in city centre and near temple.
internet_connectivity: Good 4G and broadband.
nearest_airport_name: Sri Guru Ram Dass Jee International Airport, Amritsar
peak_tourist_season: October-March and festival times (Gurpurab, Baisakhi, Diwali)
off_season: Peak summer and some monsoon weeks
rainfall_pattern: Typical Punjab monsoon with heavy showers in July-August.
food_scene: Rich Punjabi cuisine from dhabas to sit-down restaurants; vegetarian and non-vegetarian options.
local_culture: Strong Sikh heritage mixed with Punjabi urban culture.
local_customs: Cover head, remove shoes and wash feet before entering temple complex; maintain silence and decorum.
festivals_events: Gurpurab celebrations, Baisakhi, Diwali at Golden Temple and national days at border.
unique_experiences: 24-hour open Golden Temple complex with community kitchen feeding thousands daily, combined with patriotic Wagah Border ceremony.
activities_available: Heritage and food walks in old city
avoid_seasons: Hottest months (May-June) for mid-day sightseeing; foggy winter mornings for long drives

road_connectivity: Hilly road from Chamba-Mussoorie side with moderate traffic; accessible by car, taxi and limited buses.
atm_availability: Few ATMs on route; better to withdraw in Mussoorie/Chamba.
internet_connectivity: Improving 4G; many stays advertise work-friendly Wi-Fi but speeds can vary.
off_season: Mid-monsoon weeks and very cold snaps
rainfall_pattern: Regular Himalayan monsoon with misty days and occasional road disruption.
food_scene: Mostly in-house meals at stays and a few dhabas; simple North Indian and Garhwali food.
local_culture: Garhwali villages with traditional hill lifestyle.
local_customs: Respect village privacy and temple norms; ask before entering orchards.
festivals_events: Local temple fairs; main draw is calm nature.
unique_experiences: Quiet hill hamlet above Mussoorie with orchards and limited commercialisation, popular as a peaceful workation spot.
avoid_seasons: Days of heavy snowfall or landslide alerts in peak winter and monsoon.

road_connectivity: Mountain roads from Almora side; last stretch into Binsar Wildlife Sanctuary has controlled vehicle entry.
atm_availability: ATMs in Almora; none inside sanctuary.
internet_connectivity: Variable; some properties have decent Wi-Fi, others very limited.
permits_details: Forest entry ticket for sanctuary gate; charged per vehicle/person.
off_season: Monsoon months and some deep winter weeks
rainfall_pattern: Good monsoon rainfall keeps forest lush; mist is common.
food_scene: Mostly in-house food at lodges/homestays; Kumaoni dishes plus simple North Indian.
local_culture: Kumaoni hill culture with small villages and terrace farming.
local_customs: Keep noise low in forest; respect village privacy.
festivals_events: Local hill festivals in nearby towns; Binsar itself is nature-focused.
unique_experiences: Staying inside or near a forest sanctuary with dense oak-rhododendron woods and Himalayan peak views from ridges.
avoid_seasons: Peak monsoon when leeches and slippery trails are common; heavy snowfall spells if roads close.

road_connectivity: Long, winding mountain roads via Almora-Thal or other Kumaon routes; scenic but time-consuming.
atm_availability: Limited; carry sufficient cash from bigger towns.
internet_connectivity: Basic 3G/4G in town; weaker as you move out.
off_season: Monsoon and deep winter
rainfall_pattern: Heavy monsoon rains; shoulder months offer greener views.
food_scene: Local eateries and in-house kitchens; Kumaoni and North Indian dishes.
local_culture: Traditional Kumaoni villages with high-mountain lifestyle.
local_customs: Ask before photographing locals; respect village boundaries and fields.
festivals_events: Local fairs; main focus is mountain and trekking culture.
unique_experiences: Front-row views of snow-clad Panchachuli range from a quiet Kumaon town known as a trekkers' base.
avoid_seasons: Peak monsoon and heavy snowfall periods when roads and high trails may close.

road_connectivity: 7-8 hour drive from Delhi via Dehradun and Vikasnagar; last sections are hilly with some narrow curves.
atm_availability: Limited; withdraw in Dehradun or larger towns.
internet_connectivity: Basic 4G in town; weaker in forest and remote hamlets.
off_season: Rainiest weeks and extreme cold spells
rainfall_pattern: Regular hill-station rain and mist in monsoon.
food_scene: Local dhabas and in-house kitchens serving simple Indian food.
local_culture: Garhwali villages with military presence in cantonment area.
local_customs: Respect cantonment rules and village boundaries.
festivals_events: Local fairs; nature remains the main draw.
unique_experiences: Quiet cantonment hill town with deodar forests and expansive Himalayan views from Deoban on clear days.
activities_available: Nature walks and birding at Deoban
Short treks to waterfalls and viewpoints
avoid_seasons: Peak monsoon and heavy snowfall days when roads get risky.

road_connectivity: Good forest highways from Jabalpur, Nagpur and Raipur to resort zones like Kisli, Mukki, Kanha.
atm_availability: ATMs in nearby towns; carry cash to lodge.
internet_connectivity: Limited mobile data in forest belt; Wi-Fi in some lodges.
permits_details: Online/office safari permits per vehicle and zone; ID proof mandatory.
off_season: Very hot late May-June days and monsoon closure
rainfall_pattern: Central Indian monsoon with park closed during peak rains.
food_scene: Mostly in-lodge buffets or set menus with Indian and some continental dishes.
local_culture: Gond and Baiga tribal communities around buffer zones.
local_customs: Respect local communities and avoid intrusive photography.
festivals_events: Local tribal and village fairs; park itself follows seasonal safari calendar.
unique_experiences: Large, biodiverse tiger reserve known for regular tiger and barasingha sightings, considered among top safari parks in India.
activities_available: Nature walks in buffer zones (where allowed)
best_seasons: October-June with peak sightings often Feb-May.
avoid_seasons: Monsoon closure when core park is shut (typically July-September).

road_connectivity: Good highway from Jaipur, Delhi side; regular trains to Sawai Madhopur then short drive to resort belt.
atm_availability: ATMs in Sawai Madhopur town.
internet_connectivity: Decent 4G in Sawai Madhopur; resort Wi-Fi near town.
permits_details: Advance online booking recommended; options for shared and exclusive vehicles; zone allocation by department.
off_season: Pre-monsoon shoulder and monsoon closure
rainfall_pattern: Semi-arid with concentrated monsoon; park closed when tracks are wet.
food_scene: Primarily resort restaurants with Rajasthani and North Indian menus.
local_culture: Rajasthani rural communities around buffer; folk arts and crafts.
local_customs: Dress modestly in villages; tip guides and drivers responsibly rather than pushing for rule-breaking.
festivals_events: Local fairs and religious festivals; special safari demand around holidays.
unique_experiences: Iconic tiger reserve where big cats are often seen near ancient ruins and lakes, part of popular Golden Triangle extensions.
activities_available: Fort and temple visits (as per rules)
best_seasons: October-April; hot months can be excellent for sightings near water.
avoid_seasons: Monsoon closure July-September.

road_connectivity: Forest and state highways from Jabalpur, Katni and Umaria to Tala and other tourism zones.
atm_availability: ATMs in Umaria/nearby towns; carry cash to park area.
internet_connectivity: Resort Wi-Fi and limited mobile data depending on location.
permits_details: Safari booking per zone/vehicle with limited seats; ID proof required.
off_season: Late summer heat and monsoon closure
rainfall_pattern: Central Indian monsoon, park shut during heavy-rain period.
food_scene: Lodge-based dining with Indian and some continental dishes.
local_culture: Rural MP villages with strong connection to forest landscape.
local_customs: Respect village life; do not pressure guides to break rules for closer sightings.
festivals_events: Local festivals; some lodges host nature and photography workshops.
unique_experiences: One of India's best-known high-density tiger reserves, often recommended for focused tiger photography tours.
best_seasons: October-June; hottest months increase chances at water holes.
avoid_seasons: Monsoon closure July-September.

road_connectivity: Good highways from Nagpur to Moharli and other gates; ~2-3 hour drive from city.
atm_availability: ATMs in Chandrapur; carry cash to lodge.
internet_connectivity: Limited mobile data; some lodges have Wi-Fi.
permits_details: Advance safari permits with zone allocations; adherence to capacity limits.
off_season: Late summer heat and monsoon closure
rainfall_pattern: Hot, dry summers; distinct monsoon closure period.
food_scene: In-resort dining with Maharashtrian and North Indian food.
local_culture: Vidarbha rural communities; some areas with strong forest dependence.
local_customs: Be respectful when visiting villages; avoid flashy photography of people without consent.
festivals_events: Local village festivals; park focuses on safari season cycle.
unique_experiences: Well-known for high probability of tiger sightings, accessible from Nagpur with diverse landscapes and water reservoirs.
activities_available: Boat safaris in some buffer waterbodies (subject to rules)
Night drives in certain buffer zones (if permitted)
best_seasons: October-June; best views often in dry months when animals visit water.
avoid_seasons: Monsoon closure July-September.

road_connectivity: Internal island roads and walking paths only; inter-island travel by boats and ships arranged through administration/tour operators.
atm_availability: Very limited; carry adequate cash as per operator guidance.
internet_connectivity: Limited; some resorts offer basic connectivity but expect digital detox.
permits_details: Entry permits issued via Lakshadweep administration and tour operators; foreigners face additional restrictions.
off_season: Monsoon months and shoulder periods with choppy seas
rainfall_pattern: Heavy monsoon with strong winds; most tourism structured outside wettest months.
food_scene: Resort and camp kitchens serving South Indian, seafood and simple continental dishes.
local_culture: Predominantly Muslim island communities with conservative norms; tourism is tightly regulated.
local_customs: Dress modestly away from resort beaches; respect no-alcohol norms and local prayer times.
festivals_events: Local Islamic festivals; tourism structured more by season than by events.
unique_experiences: Tropical atolls with turquoise lagoons and vibrant coral reefs that remain far less crowded than other Indian beach destinations.
activities_available: Snorkelling, scuba diving and kayaking in lagoons
Lagoon boat rides and reef walks
best_seasons: Dry, calm-sea months from October-March; some itineraries also run through April.
avoid_seasons: Southwest monsoon (rough seas, limited access) and cyclone-alert periods.

road_connectivity: Small internal roads within island; access via ships and boats as part of Lakshadweep itineraries.
atm_availability: None on island; payments usually arranged through package operators.
internet_connectivity: Minimal; expect near-complete digital detox.
permits_details: Same Lakshadweep entry permit regime; movement handled via official tours.
off_season: Monsoon months and rough-sea spells
rainfall_pattern: Heavy rains in monsoon; tourism structured around dry months.
food_scene: Set meals within packages, featuring South Indian staples and fresh seafood.
local_culture: Small Muslim island community with traditional lifestyle.
local_customs: Dress modestly away from tourist-beach areas; follow island administration guidelines.
festivals_events: Local religious observances; tourism is quiet and nature-focused.
unique_experiences: Lagoon-focused island dubbed a 'lagoon of wonders' with shallow, wide lagoons ideal for non-swimmers and gentle water activities.
activities_available: Snorkelling and basic diving experiences (where offered)
best_seasons: October-March when seas are calmer and lagoons easily accessible.
avoid_seasons: Monsoon and stormy periods when boat connectivity and activities are restricted.

road_connectivity: Good highways from Jodhpur and Bikaner; buses and cabs available, desert stretches beyond town by road/jeep.

internet_connectivity: Good 4G in town; weaker at remote dune camps.
peak_tourist_season: November-February and during Jaisalmer Desert Festival dates in February.
off_season: April-September (very hot; some camps shut in off months)
rainfall_pattern: Very low rainfall desert climate; rare but intense showers possible in monsoon.

local_culture: Desert trading and warrior heritage with strong folk-art traditions.

unique_experiences: Golden sandstone fort city rising from Thar Desert with dune safaris and stargazing at desert camps.
avoid_seasons: Peak summer for extreme heat; occasional dust storms; check festival crowd levels if seeking quiet.

road_connectivity: Good roads from Bhuj to Mandvi, Kala Dungar and craft villages like Hodka, Nirona and Bhujodi.
atm_availability: ATMs in Bhuj and Mandvi; carry cash to villages.
internet_connectivity: Good in Bhuj and Mandvi; weaker in remote villages.
peak_tourist_season: Rann Utsav months and long weekends
off_season: Hot off-peak months and monsoon
rainfall_pattern: Semi-arid with light to moderate monsoon rainfall.

unique_experiences: Mix of palaces, coastal beaches and famous artisan villages producing textiles, Rogan art and embroidery, complementing White Rann visits.
accommodation_types: Heritage and beach resorts near Mandvi
avoid_seasons: Peak summer afternoons and humid monsoon days; some craft activity slows in extreme weather.

rainfall_pattern: Heavy southwest monsoon leading to lush valleys and full waterfalls.

local_customs: Respect estate rules; ask before entering fields or photographing workers.

avoid_seasons: Hottest pre-monsoon days for mid-day outings; peak heavy-rain spells if you dislike constant showers.

road_connectivity: Ghat roads from Kozhikode, Mysuru and Kannur; well-used by buses and private vehicles.

local_customs: Respect tribal village boundaries and ask before entering/photographing.
festivals_events: Local temple and church festivals; monsoon and Onam periods have special festivities.

best_seasons: Post-monsoon to winter (October-February) and early monsoon for greenery.
avoid_seasons: Heaviest monsoon days due to landslide and waterfall-risk alerts, especially in Ghat sections.

road_connectivity: Scenic but winding Ghat road connecting Pune-Mulshi-Tamhini-Konkan; popular monsoon drive route.

internet_connectivity: Mobile data workable at many points; weaker in deeper ghat sections.
off_season: Dry summer weeks with less greenery
rainfall_pattern: Very high rainfall in monsoon; frequent low clouds and fog; flash-flood risk in heavy spells.
food_scene: Roadside dhabas and resorts serving Maharashtrian and multi-cuisine meals.
local_culture: Rural Maharashtrian villages and farming communities.
local_customs: Keep noise low in villages; avoid littering or drinking in public near residents.
festivals_events: Ganesh Chaturthi and local temple fairs; monsoon itself is treated as a seasonal celebration.
unique_experiences: Lush Ghat drive with numerous small waterfalls and forested curves, considered a hidden gem compared to crowded Lonavala routes.
avoid_seasons: Days with red or orange heavy-rain alerts in Ghat sections due to landslide and flood risk.

road_connectivity: Good hill roads from Pune and Mumbai; many buses and cabs; some curves and fog in monsoon.
atm_availability: ATMs in Mahabaleshwar and Panchgani.
internet_connectivity: Good in towns and many resorts.
peak_tourist_season: December-May weekends and summers for families
off_season: Some monsoon weeks with heavy rain
rainfall_pattern: Very high monsoon rainfall; frequent fog reduces visibility.

local_culture: Maharashtrian hill communities with tourism-oriented economy.
local_customs: Standard hill-town etiquette; respect private farms and do not pluck without permission.
festivals_events: Strawberry festival and local temple events; weekend rush often feels festive.
unique_experiences: Classic Western Ghats hill station with cliff-edge viewpoints, strawberries and misty monsoon drives.
best_seasons: Strawberry and winter season (November-February); monsoon for foggy, green landscapes.
avoid_seasons: Peak holiday weekends when traffic jams around narrow roads become intense; heavy-rain red-alert days for landslide risk.

road_connectivity: Good highways from Bengaluru and Mangaluru; last stretches into hill estates via narrow roads.
atm_availability: ATMs in Chikmagalur town; limited in outskirts.
internet_connectivity: Good 4G in town, variable in remote estates.
off_season: Some monsoon weeks; weekdays see fewer crowds
rainfall_pattern: Substantial monsoon rainfall adds mist and full waterfalls.
food_scene: Homely Karnataka food in stays plus small restaurants in town; excellent filter coffee.
local_culture: Coffee-growing communities with mix of plantations and villages.
local_customs: Ask before entering estate tracks; keep noise low in villages and forests.
festivals_events: Local temple festivals and hill fairs.
unique_experiences: High hills of the Western Ghats mixing coffee country with some of Karnataka's most popular trekking peaks.
activities_available: Jeep rides to falls or peaks
best_seasons: Post-monsoon to winter for trekking; early monsoon for lush scenery.
avoid_seasons: Very heavy-rain days where landslides or trail closures occur; peak summer afternoons for strenuous treks.

road_connectivity: Ghat road connecting Belagavi region with Konkan via Amboli; popular monsoon route with buses and cars.

internet_connectivity: Basic mobile data in town; weak in inner forest sections.

rainfall_pattern: One of Maharashtra's wettest ghats with persistent rain and fog in peak season.
food_scene: Simple Maharashtrian and Konkan dishes in local eateries.
local_culture: Konkan-Maharashtra hill communities; agriculture and small tourism.
local_customs: Respect local advice on safe waterfall access; dress modestly in village areas.
festivals_events: Local temple festivals; monsoon weekends effectively become an event for visitors.
unique_experiences: Very wet hill station that becomes a 'mist and waterfalls' destination in monsoon, with interest from herp enthusiasts for endemic frogs and reptiles.
activities_available: Monsoon walks near viewpoints and falls
best_seasons: Monsoon months (June-September) for full waterfalls and mist; shoulder months for calmer weather.
avoid_seasons: Extremely heavy-rain alert days with landslide or road-closure risk; respect all IMD alerts.

road_connectivity: Hairpin Ghat roads from Udupi/Mangaluru side and interior Karnataka; buses and cabs available.
atm_availability: ATMs in larger nearby towns; none in deep interior.
internet_connectivity: Limited; consider stay as semi-digital-detox.
permits_details: Forest department permissions for treks and some viewpoints; local homestays often arrange.
peak_tourist_season: Monsoon weekends for enthusiasts; winter for general trekking
off_season: Hotter pre-monsoon weeks
rainfall_pattern: Extremely high rainfall; frequent downpours and low clouds.
food_scene: Simple home-style Karnataka and coastal-influenced meals at homestays.
local_culture: Rural Western Ghats communities with agriculture and forest-linked livelihoods.
