festivals_events: Local temple festivals; scientific events related to rainforest research occasionally.
unique_experiences: One of India's wettest regions with dense rainforests, king cobra research area and dramatic Ghats sunsets.
activities_available: Forest treks with guides (permits as required)
Monsoon and post-monsoon herping and macro photography
best_seasons: Monsoon and immediately after (June-October) for rainforest atmosphere; winter for drier treks.
avoid_seasons: Severe weather spells with official landslide/flood alerts; some trails are closed in heavy monsoon.

road_connectivity: Ghat roads from Mangaluru, Chikmagalur and Sringeri with forest check-posts and regulated access to national park area.
atm_availability: ATMs in larger towns before entering interior belt.
internet_connectivity: Limited; some homestays have basic network coverage.
permits_details: Trek permits and visitor limits per day; issued via forest department/registered homestays.
off_season: Peak monsoon and hottest pre-monsoon days
rainfall_pattern: Very high rainfall during monsoon; lush greenery and strong streams afterwards.
food_scene: Simple, hearty home-cooked Karnataka meals at homestays.
local_culture: Farming and plantation villages in Western Ghats foothills.
local_customs: Respect homestay rules and quiet hours; no alcohol or loud music in forest zones.
festivals_events: Local temple festivals; nature is main draw.
unique_experiences: Iconic horse-face shaped mountain amid grassland-forest mosaic, considered one of Karnataka's most beautiful treks.
activities_available: Full-day guided treks to Kudremukh peak (with permits)
best_seasons: Post-monsoon (October-February) for clear views; monsoon for dramatic clouds but restricted trekking windows.
avoid_seasons: Days with heavy rain/landslide alerts; core trek often closed or controlled during worst monsoon spells.

road_connectivity: Internal island roads for local travel by cabs, autos, bikes and cycles; main access is ferry from Port Blair.
atm_availability: Limited; withdraw cash in Port Blair and carry cards accepted by many resorts.
internet_connectivity: Improving but still patchy; many visitors treat it as partial digital detox.
permits_details: Standard Andaman entry formalities via Port Blair; additional restricted-area permits not usually needed for Indians on Havelock itself.
peak_tourist_season: December-March and around New Year/long weekends.
off_season: Low monsoon months and exam/off-peak periods
rainfall_pattern: Tropical maritime climate with heavy spells during southwest and retreating monsoons.
food_scene: Seafood-centric menus plus Indian and some continental cafes; resort dining is common.
local_culture: Settler communities with mixed mainland Indian backgrounds; island economy heavily tourism-dependent.
local_customs: Respect beach codes, avoid alcohol on public beaches in sensitive areas, and adhere to 'no-touch' rules for corals.
festivals_events: Local versions of mainland festivals; tourism events peak in high season.
unique_experiences: White-sand beaches with clear teal water and rich reefs, often considered India's flagship tropical-island experience.
activities_available: Sea walks and glass-bottom boat rides
best_seasons: November-April with calm seas and good visibility; shoulder months around October and early May can also work.
avoid_seasons: Peak monsoon and rough-sea periods when ferries may be disrupted and many activities shut.

road_connectivity: Small internal network of roads and village lanes; accessed via ferries from Port Blair and Havelock.
atm_availability: Very limited; most travellers carry cash from Port Blair.
internet_connectivity: Even patchier than Havelock; assume low-speed or intermittent connectivity.
permits_details: Covered under standard Andaman entry regime via Port Blair; tour operators handle logistics.
peak_tourist_season: December-March but still less crowded than Havelock.
off_season: Monsoon and low-traffic shoulder months
rainfall_pattern: Same Andaman tropical monsoon regime with heavy showers and cloudbursts.
food_scene: Simple island cafes and resort restaurants; seafood and Indian staples dominate.
local_culture: Laid-back island communities engaged in tourism, fishing and small-scale farming.
local_customs: Modest beachwear away from main tourist zones; courteous interaction with locals.
festivals_events: No major unique festival; atmosphere is always quiet and village-like.
unique_experiences: Smaller, calmer island than Havelock with relaxed vibe, shallow lagoons and quaint rural scenery.
best_seasons: November-April for clear seas; can be combined with Havelock in a single itinerary.
avoid_seasons: Rough monsoon sea periods that disrupt ferries; some beaches may be unsafe for swimming then.

road_connectivity: Town roads with taxis, autos and rented two-wheelers; primary gateway by flights and ships from mainland.
atm_availability: Multiple ATMs and banks across town.
internet_connectivity: Best internet in Andamans but still slower than mainland; 4G improving.
nearest_airport_name: Veer Savarkar International Airport, Port Blair
permits_details: Standard entry process at airport; Restricted Area Permit regime is integrated into arrival for most Indian tourists.
off_season: Monsoon and lower-traffic shoulder months
rainfall_pattern: Heavy tropical rains; sightseeing sometimes rearranged around showers.
food_scene: Mix of South Indian, North Indian and seafood restaurants plus bakeries and cafes.
local_culture: Multi-ethnic island capital with diverse communities and seafaring orientation.
local_customs: Photography may be restricted in some government/defence areas; follow posted signs.
festivals_events: National days are marked strongly at Cellular Jail; local versions of mainland festivals.
unique_experiences: Historic port town that frames Andaman's freedom-struggle narrative while acting as the logistics hub for island-hopping.
best_seasons: October-April aligning with Andaman high season.
avoid_seasons: Rough-sea monsoon spells that affect boat operations and outdoor sightseeing.

road_connectivity: Hill roads and shared jeeps from Siliguri/NJP/Bagdogra; iconic Darjeeling Himalayan Railway operates on a narrow-gauge route.
atm_availability: ATMs in town centre and nearby areas.
internet_connectivity: Good 4G in town; weaker in remote tea estates.
peak_tourist_season: Summer holidays (April-June) and Durga Puja/Diwali periods.
off_season: Deep monsoon and some mid-winter weeks
rainfall_pattern: Heavy monsoon rains affect road conditions and visibility.
food_scene: North Indian, Tibetan, Nepali and continental cafes and bakeries.
local_culture: Gorkha-majority hill culture with Tibetan and Bengali influences.
local_customs: Respect monastery rules and avoid loud behaviour in residential hill lanes.
festivals_events: Local hill festivals and pan-Indian celebrations; tea plucking seasons add interest.
unique_experiences: Colonial-era hill station with UNESCO-listed Himalayan Railway and world-famous tea estates facing the Eastern Himalayas.
best_seasons: March-June and October-November for views and pleasant weather.
avoid_seasons: Peak monsoon for landslide risks and clouded views; some winter weeks can be very cold and foggy.

road_connectivity: Mountain roads from Siliguri/NJP via Teesta valley; shared cabs and private taxis common.
atm_availability: Multiple ATMs and banks in town.
internet_connectivity: Good 4G coverage in city; weaker in outlying areas.
permits_details: Inner Line/Protected Area permits for specific excursions and for foreign nationals in many parts of Sikkim.
peak_tourist_season: Summer vacations and Durga Puja/Diwali corridors.
off_season: Deep monsoon and some winter weeks
rainfall_pattern: High rainfall in monsoon; frequent cloud and mist on valley roads.
food_scene: Combination of Tibetan, Nepali and Indian dishes plus modern cafes.
local_culture: Blend of Lepcha, Bhutia and Nepali influences with strong Buddhist presence.
local_customs: Dress modestly for monastery visits and maintain silence inside prayer halls.
festivals_events: Losar, Saga Dawa and other Buddhist festivals, plus pan-Indian celebrations.
unique_experiences: Clean, organised hill capital acting as a base for wider Sikkim exploration with strong Buddhist influence and valley views.
activities_available: Day trips to Tsomgo Lake and Nathu La (if open)
accommodation_types: Hotels and boutique stays in town
best_seasons: March-June and October-December for clear views and comfortable temperatures.
avoid_seasons: Peak monsoon for landslide risk; some high passes close in winter due to snow.

road_connectivity: Narrow mountain roads from Gangtok with landslide-prone sections; only authorised vehicles with permits allowed for tourists.
atm_availability: ATMs mainly in Gangtok; carry cash for North Sikkim.
internet_connectivity: Very limited; assume low/no mobile data in many stretches.
permits_details: Special permits via registered tour operators; foreign nationals have more restrictions near border belts.
peak_tourist_season: April-June (flower season) and October holiday weeks.
off_season: Monsoon and harshest winter weeks
rainfall_pattern: Heavy; roads frequently affected in rainy periods.
food_scene: Simple set meals at lodges/homestays; mostly Indian and local hill dishes.
local_culture: Highland Buddhist and rural Sikkimese communities.
local_customs: Respect army presence and photography restrictions near border/strategic areas.
festivals_events: Local monastery festivals; tourism is more seasonal than event-centric.
unique_experiences: High-altitude valleys with dramatic landscapes, rhododendron blooms in season and glimpses of Himalayan peaks, accessed via staged overnight trips.
best_seasons: Spring (April-June) for blooms; autumn and early winter for clearer views.
avoid_seasons: Peak monsoon (landslides, closures) and severe winter spells when access to Gurudongmar/Yumthang can be cut off.

road_connectivity: Good highways from Guwahati to Shillong and on to Sohra (Cherrapunji) and Dawki; shared cabs and taxis widely used.
atm_availability: ATMs in Shillong and main towns; limited in smaller villages.
internet_connectivity: Good in Shillong; patchy in interior villages but improving.
peak_tourist_season: Winter holidays and March-April shoulder season.
off_season: Monsoon for mainstream tourists (though some enthusiasts visit for raw rain experience)
rainfall_pattern: Among world's wettest zones around Sohra/Mawsynram; rainfall shapes entire tourism pattern.
food_scene: Mix of Khasi cuisine, North Indian and cafe food; pork and local specialties for non-vegetarians.
local_culture: Khasi matrilineal communities with strong village councils and church presence.
local_customs: Obey village rules for trekking routes and photograph people only with consent.
festivals_events: Local religious and harvest festivals; Christmas season is festive across Meghalaya.
unique_experiences: Cloud-laced cliffs, intense waterfalls and indigenous Khasi engineering in the living root bridges, plus glassy rivers in season.
activities_available: Boating on Umngot River at Dawki (seasonal clarity)
accommodation_types: Homestays and small resorts around Sohra and Mawlynnong
best_seasons: October-April; post-monsoon brings full waterfalls with safer access, winter offers clearer skies.
avoid_seasons: Heaviest monsoon months for landslides and dangerous waterfall conditions; some caves/rivers swell dangerously.

destination_name: Kaziranga National Park & Assam Tea Belt
road_connectivity: NH27 and other highways link Guwahati and upper Assam to Kaziranga; good road conditions outside flood events.
atm_availability: ATMs in nearby towns and along main highway.
internet_connectivity: Lodge Wi-Fi and basic mobile data near highway; weaker deeper inside greenery.
permits_details: Safari permits and range allocations managed by forest department; bookings via lodges and agents.
off_season: Early/late shoulder around opening/closing months
rainfall_pattern: Heavy monsoon rains cause seasonal flooding, crucial to ecology but limiting access.
food_scene: Lodge buffets with Assamese and Indian dishes; simple fare in nearby towns.
local_culture: Assamese villages with strong tea-industry presence and Brahmaputra floodplain lifestyle.
local_customs: Respect local village customs and dress modestly in rural areas.
festivals_events: Bihu festivals in Assam; some lodges offer cultural evenings.
unique_experiences: UNESCO-listed floodplain ecosystem famous for its rhino population alongside elephants, deer and rich birdlife, often combined with Assam tea-garden stays.
activities_available: Morning and afternoon safaris in different ranges
best_seasons: November-April, with pleasant winter temperatures and good sightings.
avoid_seasons: Monsoon (park closed typically from May/June to October due to Brahmaputra floods).

road_connectivity: Highways connect Khajuraho with Jhansi, Satna and Panna; local roads lead to Panna National Park gates.
atm_availability: ATMs in Khajuraho town and nearby urban centres.
internet_connectivity: Good in Khajuraho; patchy nearer park interior.
permits_details: Safari permits for Panna ranges; temple visits need only entry tickets.
peak_tourist_season: Winter months and around festival/holiday periods.
off_season: Hot summer and some monsoon weeks
rainfall_pattern: Central Indian monsoon with heavy but seasonal rains.
food_scene: Indian restaurants and hotel dining; simple options near park gate.
local_culture: Bundelkhand region with mix of rural communities and temple-town economy.
local_customs: Dress modestly in temple areas; remove footwear where required.
festivals_events: Khajuraho Dance Festival and religious festivals enliven temple precincts.
unique_experiences: Rare combination of world-famous temple art and a nearby tiger reserve in a single, compact circuit.
best_seasons: October-March for comfortable sightseeing and safaris; shoulder months for warmer but quieter travel.
avoid_seasons: Peak summer afternoons for temple visits; monsoon when park access and river levels fluctuate.

road_connectivity: Short drive from Jhansi via good roads; well linked to Gwalior, Khajuraho and other Bundelkhand routes.
atm_availability: ATMs in Orchha and nearby Jhansi.
internet_connectivity: Decent 4G coverage in town.
peak_tourist_season: Winter, especially around long weekends and festivals.
off_season: Summer and mid-monsoon periods
rainfall_pattern: Monsoon rains can swell Betwa and make banks slippery.
food_scene: Simple local restaurants and hotel dining, mainly Indian cuisine.
local_culture: Religious and heritage town with strong Ram devotion and Bundelkhand traditions.
local_customs: Dress modestly at temples; evenings near Ram Raja Temple can be quite devotional.
festivals_events: Ram-related festivals draw pilgrims; light-and-sound shows and cultural programmes sometimes held at fort.
unique_experiences: Compact heritage town with palaces and riverside cenotaphs that feel quieter and less commercial than many big-name sites.
best_seasons: October-March for pleasant days and comfortable walks.
avoid_seasons: Peak summer heat in afternoons; monsoon high river levels for certain water activities.

road_connectivity: Well-connected by coastal highways and buses from Goa, Mangaluru and Bengaluru; last stretch to beaches by auto/taxi or on foot.
atm_availability: ATMs in town; limited options near remote beaches.
internet_connectivity: Decent 4G in town and main beaches; some homestays promote workation stays with Wi-Fi.
off_season: Monsoon and exam months with many budget places discounted
rainfall_pattern: Strong Konkan monsoon with frequent showers and rough surf.
food_scene: Mix of coastal Karnataka, North Indian and continental cafes with many vegetarian-friendly options.
local_culture: Pilgrimage town with a simple coastal lifestyle; visitors share space with devotees and fishing communities.
local_customs: Dress modestly inside town and temples; remove footwear where required.
festivals_events: Religious festivals at Mahabaleshwar Temple and local temple fairs; New Year sees more backpacker gatherings.
unique_experiences: Laid-back temple town with a string of coves where homestays and shacks sit just off the sand, offering a quieter alternative to Goa.
best_seasons: November-March for pleasant weather and calmer seas.
avoid_seasons: Peak monsoon for rough seas and many shacks closing; May heat can be intense mid-day.

road_connectivity: Hill roads from Kathgodam/Haldwani with regular buses and shared cabs; Almora is a key hub for nearby valleys like Binsar and Kasar Devi.
atm_availability: ATMs in Almora town; none on remote ridges.
internet_connectivity: 4G in town; variable along ridge and interiors but many cafes provide workable Wi-Fi.
off_season: Mid-monsoon and shoulder periods when some cafes shut
rainfall_pattern: Typical mid-Himalayan monsoon with some road disruption on very heavy days.
food_scene: Simple Kumaoni and North Indian food plus traveller cafes on ridge serving basics and coffee.
local_culture: Traditional Kumaoni families, temples and old bazaar traditions mixed with newer alternative/creative communities.
local_customs: Dress modestly near temples and in old-town lanes; support local shops for snacks and essentials.
festivals_events: Local temple fairs and standard hill festivals; occasional retreats/workshops around Kasar.
unique_experiences: Relaxed Kumaon hill town with a historic bazaar core and a ridge (Kasar Devi) long associated with writers, seekers and spiritual travellers.
activities_available: Short drives to viewpoints and Binsar gate
accommodation_types: Homestays and small resorts on surrounding hills
best_seasons: October-April for crisp views; monsoon for lush valleys if okay with cloud.
avoid_seasons: Peak monsoon landslide alerts and coldest snaps if not prepared for low temperatures.

road_connectivity: Long, winding Himalayan roads via Sela Pass; travel usually broken into stages (Guwahati-Bomdila/Dirang-Tawang).
atm_availability: ATMs in larger towns like Bomdila/Tawang but can run out of cash; carry reserves.
internet_connectivity: Limited; expect slow data and patchy coverage.
permits_details: ILP for Arunachal plus special permits for some border areas; typically arranged from Guwahati/online.
peak_tourist_season: April-May and October festive season; also popular in winter for snow trips.
off_season: Heavy monsoon period and mid-winter cold snaps
rainfall_pattern: High rainfall in monsoon; snow in winter around passes and occasionally town.
food_scene: Simple Tibetan, North Indian and local Arunachali dishes; mostly homely meals.
local_culture: Monpa Buddhist communities with monasteries and traditional houses.
local_customs: Be respectful in monasteries and around army installations; photography may be restricted.
festivals_events: Losar and monastery festivals; military parades on national days.
unique_experiences: Remote Himalayan Buddhist town near the China border with a major monastery and stark, beautiful landscapes.
activities_available: Scenic drives to lakes and passes
best_seasons: March-May and October-November for clear skies; January for snow for those prepared for cold.
avoid_seasons: Peak monsoon for landslides; some deep winter spells for road closures and extreme cold.

road_connectivity: Seasonal high mountain roads via Shimla-Kinnaur or Manali-Rohtang-Kunzum; often open only from late spring to early autumn.
atm_availability: ATMs in Kaza may not always be stocked; carry sufficient cash.
internet_connectivity: Spotty; some BSNL and limited 4G in Kaza and a few villages; expect digital detox.
permits_details: Inner Line Permits for some foreign travellers and for sensitive border stretches; check latest regulations.
peak_tourist_season: July-September; becoming popular with backpackers and road-trippers.
off_season: Early and late shoulder weeks; winter is only for expedition-level visits
rainfall_pattern: Rain-shadow region; minimal rainfall but neighbouring Kinnaur/Manali roads can see landslides.
food_scene: Simple Indian and Tibetan dishes; supplies more limited than mainstream hill stations.
local_culture: Buddhist villages with agriculture and pastoralism; monasteries central to community life.
local_customs: Respect monastery etiquette and ask before photographing people.
festivals_events: Local monastery festivals and masked dances, mainly in summer.
unique_experiences: Trans-Himalayan cold desert with dramatic moonscapes, ancient monasteries and minimal vegetation, offering a semi-Ladakh feel in Himachal.
accommodation_types: Guesthouses in Kaza and key villages
best_seasons: June-September for full circuit access; May and October in lower sections depending on snow.
avoid_seasons: Winter and early spring when many roads/villages are cut off and temperatures plunge.

road_connectivity: Road from Aut tunnel on Chandigarh-Manali highway into Tirthan and Jibhi region; regular buses to Aut, then local taxis.
atm_availability: ATMs at Aut/Banjar; limited in deeper villages.
internet_connectivity: Improving 4G; many stays advertise workable Wi-Fi, but speeds vary by village.
off_season: Mid-monsoon (except for slow travellers okay with storms)
rainfall_pattern: Himalayan monsoon with swelling streams and lush forests.
food_scene: Homely Himachali food and simple cafes serving Indian and continental dishes.
local_culture: Himachali villages with agriculture, orchards and small-scale tourism.
local_customs: Ask before entering fields or photographing homes; keep music volume low at night.
festivals_events: Local fairs and temple festivals; valley retains traditional rhythms.
unique_experiences: Peaceful valley with cedar forests, wooden homes and riverside stays, popular among backpackers escaping Manali crowds.
activities_available: Short treks to waterfalls and viewpoints
best_seasons: March-June and September-November for pleasant weather; winter for snow in higher reaches.
avoid_seasons: Days of heavy monsoon landslides and peak winter road closures around Jalori and high passes.

road_connectivity: Long Himalayan drive via Shimla-Rampur-Sangla-Chitkul; roads narrow and landslide-prone in sections.
atm_availability: ATMs in bigger towns like Sangla/Recong Peo; none in Chitkul.
internet_connectivity: Very limited; assume low or no mobile data.
off_season: Early spring and late autumn with fewer visitors but colder nights
rainfall_pattern: Moderate precipitation; heavy snow in winter and snow/rain mix in shoulder months.
food_scene: Basic Himachali/North Indian set meals at lodges and dhabas.
local_culture: Kinnauri communities with distinct architecture and temples.
local_customs: Respect temple areas and avoid entering fields without consent.
festivals_events: Local village festivals at temples; seasons drive activity more than big events.
unique_experiences: End-of-the-road village with stone-and-wood houses, roaring river and close snow peaks, often cited as among Himachal's prettiest settlements.
activities_available: Photography of peaks and traditional houses
best_seasons: May-October (excluding peak monsoon) for access and green or post-monsoon views.
avoid_seasons: Deep winter for heavy snow and road closures; peak monsoon for landslides.

road_connectivity: Accessed via Manali-Rohtang/Atal Tunnel into Lahaul and then side roads/jeep tracks; limited public transport, often arranged via trek operators.
atm_availability: ATMs only in larger towns before entering valley region.
internet_connectivity: Minimal to none once inside valley.
peak_tourist_season: Short Himalayan summer; crowding is limited due to remoteness.
off_season: Most of the year outside core season
rainfall_pattern: Lies in rain-shadow-like conditions but approaches can see rain/snow; weather changeable.
food_scene: Basic; trek kitchens and homestay meals based on local staples.
local_culture: Sparse high-altitude communities with mixed Himalayan influences.
local_customs: Travel respectfully; homestays may have very simple facilities-adjust expectations.
festivals_events: Local village festivities; valley primarily a trekker's destination.
unique_experiences: Remote valley that combines elements of Himachal and Ladakh landscapes, still far less visited than popular Himalayan circuits.
activities_available: Exploration of side valleys with guides
best_seasons: July-September for trekking and open-valley access.
avoid_seasons: Winter and shoulder seasons when snow blocks routes; monsoon storms can still affect approach roads.

road_connectivity: Just off the Delhi-Agra-Jaipur Golden Triangle highways; easy access by car, bus and train.
atm_availability: ATMs in Bharatpur town.
internet_connectivity: Good 4G near town and lodges; less reliable deeper in park.
permits_details: Entry tickets at gate; no special permits needed for most Indians and foreign tourists beyond fee payment.
off_season: Summer months; monsoon is quieter though some residents remain
rainfall_pattern: Seasonal monsoon regenerates wetlands; water levels crucial to bird life.
food_scene: Hotel restaurants and local dhabas; simple North Indian and Rajasthani fare.
local_culture: Small-town Rajasthan with agriculture around wetland.
local_customs: Respect park rules, keep noise low and stay on designated paths.
festivals_events: Birding festivals and events occasionally organised; best experiences revolve around migration season.
unique_experiences: Compact UNESCO-listed bird sanctuary offering close, easy bird views in a semi-arid landscape turned wetland oasis.
activities_available: Birdwatching by cycle, on foot or cycle-rickshaw
accommodation_types: Hotels and lodges near park gate
best_seasons: October-March for winter migrants, with peak diversity in mid-winter.
avoid_seasons: Peak summer heat and mid-monsoon when bird numbers and comfort drop.

road_connectivity: Just off the Mysuru-Bengaluru highway; easy stop on road trips or day trips from Mysuru.
atm_availability: ATMs in Srirangapatna and Mysuru.
internet_connectivity: Highway and nearby towns have good 4G.
permits_details: Entry tickets and separate boat-ride charges; no special permits.
peak_tourist_season: Weekends in winter; combines with Mysuru and Srirangapatna visits.
off_season: Non-breeding months and hot seasons
rainfall_pattern: Kaveri-fed wetland with seasonal fluctuations depending on monsoon.
food_scene: Basic snacks and nearby eateries; most visitors eat in Mysuru or along highway.
local_culture: Part of Kaveri river landscape near historic Srirangapatna.
local_customs: Respect sanctuary rules and quiet environment.
festivals_events: None specific; birding itself peaks in winter.
unique_experiences: Compact wetland where breeding waterbirds nest on islets, offering close viewing from boats, ideal for a few hours' birding.
accommodation_types: Day-trip only; stay in nearby Mysuru or highway resorts
best_seasons: December-March for peak nesting and bird activity.
avoid_seasons: Peak summer afternoons for heat; flood periods when river levels are high.

road_connectivity: Connected by good roads from Ahmedabad; popular as a winter day trip by car or taxi.
atm_availability: ATMs in nearby towns and on Ahmedabad side; none inside sanctuary.
internet_connectivity: Mobile data available near entry and along approach roads.
permits_details: Entry tickets plus separate boating charges; no complex permits.
peak_tourist_season: Winter weekends and holidays; popular with local families and photographers.
off_season: Non-winter months
rainfall_pattern: Seasonal monsoon fills and refreshes wetland; bird visitors follow water and food cycles.
food_scene: Snack stalls and small eateries; most visitors plan main meals in Ahmedabad or highway dhabas.
local_culture: Wetland used traditionally by local communities; many boatmen come from nearby villages.
local_customs: Use designated entry points and follow sanctuary rules; no loud music.
festivals_events: Occasional birding events and nature camps in winter.
unique_experiences: Expansive wetland that transforms into a major winter bird haven with flamingos, pelicans and other waterbirds.
activities_available: Short walks on islets where allowed
accommodation_types: Usually day-trip only; overnight options are in Ahmedabad or small lodges nearby
best_seasons: November-February when migratory birds peak and temperatures are pleasant.
avoid_seasons: Hot summer and heavy monsoon when bird numbers and comfort decline.

road_connectivity: Good roads from Bhuj to Dhordo and beyond; desert roads are mostly paved with final stretches controlled by border/security checkposts.
atm_availability: ATMs in Bhuj and larger Kutch towns; carry cash to desert camps.
internet_connectivity: 4G in Bhuj and patchy but improving near festival zones; camps often provide Wi-Fi.
permits_details: Rann entry permit and ID often checked at Bhirandiyara/Dhordo checkpoints due to proximity to international border.
peak_tourist_season: December-January around festivals, New Year and full-moon event dates.
off_season: Non-festival months and hotter shoulder periods
rainfall_pattern: Arid to semi-arid; monsoon turns the salt desert into a shallow marsh before drying out again.
food_scene: Gujarati thalis and snacks in camps and local eateries, with simple vegetarian-heavy menus.
local_culture: Kutchi communities renowned for textiles, embroidery, folk music and desert pastoral traditions.
local_customs: Dress modestly in villages, ask before photographing people or crafts, and bargain respectfully.
festivals_events: Rann Utsav (White Desert Festival) typically runs from Nov-Feb with nightly cultural programmes.
unique_experiences: One of the world's largest salt deserts, turning into a shimmering white expanse in the dry season and hosting the colourful Rann Utsav near Dhordo.
activities_available: Cultural performances and handicraft bazaars (during festival)
Camel carts and simple desert activities
Short trips to Mandvi coast and local villages
best_seasons: November-February, coinciding with Rann Utsav and cooler desert weather; full-moon nights are especially striking.
avoid_seasons: Peak summer and monsoon when flats are marshy or waterlogged and heat is severe.

road_connectivity: Highways link Jaisalmer with Jodhpur, Jaipur and other Rajasthan cities; dunes accessed by smaller roads towards Sam and Khuri.
atm_availability: Multiple ATMs in Jaisalmer town.
internet_connectivity: Good in town; weaker but present at many larger camps.
peak_tourist_season: December-January and around Desert Festival dates, plus long-weekend spikes.
off_season: Summer and mid-monsoon when temperatures are extreme and camps may close
rainfall_pattern: Very low rainfall desert climate with occasional intense showers.
food_scene: Rajasthani and North Indian food, with many rooftop eateries overlooking fort and town.
local_culture: Rajasthani desert communities with folk music, dance and crafts forming a key part of tourist evenings.
local_customs: Dress modestly in older quarters and near temples; tipping for musicians and camel handlers is customary.
festivals_events: Jaisalmer Desert Festival and Rajasthan Desert Circuit promotions draw extra cultural programmes.
unique_experiences: Golden sandstone fort city at the edge of the Thar, combining intricate havelis with easy access to rolling sand dunes.
activities_available: Camel and jeep safaris in dunes
accommodation_types: Desert camps (ranging from basic to luxury)
best_seasons: October-March for cool desert evenings and comfortable fort exploration.
avoid_seasons: Peak summer heat and hottest pre-monsoon months; occasional dust storms.

road_connectivity: NH66 coastal highway runs beside Maravanthe with the sea on one side and river/backwaters on the other, making it an iconic self-drive stretch.
atm_availability: ATMs in Kundapura and other small towns along highway.
internet_connectivity: Good 4G along highway and in nearby towns.
peak_tourist_season: Christmas-New Year and long weekends; still quieter than major resort beaches.
off_season: Most weekdays and shoulder months, especially outside school holidays
rainfall_pattern: Heavy coastal Karnataka monsoon with strong onshore winds.
food_scene: Coastal Karnataka food with fish curries, ghee roast and simple vegetarian thalis in local eateries.
local_culture: Fishing communities and temple towns along the Karavali coast.
local_customs: Dress modestly in villages and near temples; be respectful of fishermen and their working spaces.
festivals_events: Temple festivals and annual fairs in nearby towns; not a single-event destination.
unique_experiences: Striking road section where the Arabian Sea and a river run parallel to the highway, plus little-known coves and villages ideal for unhurried stops.
activities_available: Beach walks and simple village visits
Backwater and boat experiences in nearby areas
accommodation_types: Small resorts and homestays near beach
best_seasons: November-March for calmer seas and comfortable coastal weather.
avoid_seasons: Peak monsoon for high waves and heavy rain; some erosion along highway edges occurs.

road_connectivity: Reachable by coastal roads branching from Puri-Konark-Bhubaneswar circuit; suited to taxis and self-drives.
atm_availability: ATMs in Puri, Konark and village centres, not on beachline.
internet_connectivity: Mobile data works on main approach roads; can be weaker directly on remote stretches.
peak_tourist_season: Around big festivals at Puri plus winter holiday weeks; these beaches still stay quieter than the main town.
off_season: Most non-festival weekdays and sultry pre-monsoon weeks
rainfall_pattern: Coastal monsoon with heavy showers and occasional systems in Bay of Bengal.
food_scene: Local seafood shacks and dhabas; better variety in Puri and Bhubaneswar.
local_culture: Fishing communities and temple-linked pilgrim circuits along Odisha coast.
local_customs: Ask before photographing fishermen or their catch; keep beaches clean, as waste management is limited.
festivals_events: Peak coastal energy around Rath Yatra in Puri; local village festivities at other times.
unique_experiences: Under-the-radar beaches on the Puri-Konark belt, known for vivid sunsets and relatively empty sands compared with main Puri beach.
activities_available: Watching fishing boats and village life
Combining with temple and heritage visits nearby
accommodation_types: Stays in Puri or near Konark
A few small lodges/homestays near quieter beaches
best_seasons: November-February for mild weather and calm sea views.
avoid_seasons: Cyclone-prone late-monsoon/post-monsoon periods and very hot April-May afternoons.

road_connectivity: Hilly roads from Agartala via Kailashahar/Kumarghat; improving connectivity as part of North East circuits.
atm_availability: ATMs in district towns; none at the heritage site itself.
internet_connectivity: Mobile data in towns; may be weaker within gorge area.
peak_tourist_season: Winter weeks, especially when clubbed with wider North East tours.
off_season: Hot pre-monsoon months and heavy-rain periods
rainfall_pattern: High rainfall typical of North East hilly tracts with lush vegetation.
food_scene: Local eateries with simple Bengali and Tripuri-style meals; limited variety.
local_culture: Blend of tribal and Bengali cultures, with small-farm and forest-linked lifestyles.
local_customs: Be respectful at active worship spots and avoid climbing on sculptures.
festivals_events: Local fairs and religious gatherings; Unakoti Mela draws regional visitors.
unique_experiences: Ancient rock carvings of huge faces and reliefs carved into hill slopes, set amid lush vegetation and streams, still relatively little-known outside the region.
activities_available: Village visits as part of North East circuits
accommodation_types: Basic hotels and guesthouses in nearby towns
best_seasons: November-March for comfortable temperatures and clearer skies.
avoid_seasons: Heaviest monsoon months when paths can be slippery and access affected.

road_connectivity: Excellent roads along East Coast Road (ECR) and GST corridors; frequent buses and taxis from Chennai and Puducherry.
atm_availability: ATMs available in town and along ECR.
internet_connectivity: Good 4G and broadband in town and resorts.
peak_tourist_season: Winters, weekends and festival periods; also popular for school trips.
off_season: Weekdays outside winter; some heat in shoulder seasons but manageable
rainfall_pattern: North-east monsoon influenced; short but intense spells in Oct-Dec.
food_scene: Seafood and South Indian favourites, plus cafes catering to domestic and international tourists.
local_culture: Temple town with artisans, fishermen and hospitality workers; strong Dravidian heritage.
local_customs: Dress modestly at temples; remove footwear where required.
festivals_events: Dance and cultural festivals sometimes held against heritage backdrops; nearby projects like Nandavanam Heritage Park are planned under tourism circuits.
unique_experiences: Seaside temple town with some of India's finest Pallava-era stone carving, easily combined with Chennai and Puducherry.
activities_available: Short drives to DakshinaChitra and nearby attractions
best_seasons: November-February for pleasant coastal weather; evenings are comfortable much of the year.
avoid_seasons: Peak monsoon/cyclone events and hottest April-May afternoons when humidity is high.

road_connectivity: Accessible via internal roads and short hikes/boat rides from Palolem/Agonda region; suited to cabs and two-wheelers.
atm_availability: ATMs in Canacona and other South Goa hubs.
internet_connectivity: Good 4G in nearby towns and main beaches; may be weak in certain headland spots.
peak_tourist_season: December-New Year weeks and long weekends; even then, early or weekday visits are calmer.
off_season: Most non-holiday weekdays and shoulder months like November or February end
rainfall_pattern: Heavy Konkan monsoon shuts down most shacks and sea excursions.
food_scene: Multi-cuisine shacks and cafes in main beaches; hidden coves may have nothing or one seasonal shack.
local_culture: Blend of fishing villages and tourism economy.
local_customs: Respect local fishermen's working hours and equipment stored on beaches.
festivals_events: Goa-wide festival calendar; specific coves are more about natural ambience than events.
unique_experiences: Tucked-away coves that offer a more secluded feel than many of Goa's crowded main beaches, especially on off-peak days.
activities_available: Boat trips or treks to hidden coves
accommodation_types: Beach huts and guesthouses in Palolem/Agonda
Boutique stays in South Goa interior
best_seasons: November-February for good sea conditions and pleasant weather.
avoid_seasons: Monsoon when sea is rough and many boat services stop; access trails can be slippery.

road_connectivity: Internal island roads only; external access via flights to Agatti and inter-island boats, subject to permits and schedules.
atm_availability: Very limited; payments generally arranged via packages and cards where available.
internet_connectivity: Limited; some resorts offer basic connectivity but expect partial digital detox.
permits_details: Special entry permits required for Lakshadweep; only certain islands open to tourists and often via pre-booked packages.
peak_tourist_season: December-February and national holiday blocks, though numbers are controlled.
off_season: Monsoon and shoulder months when connectivity is weather-dependent
rainfall_pattern: Tropical maritime rainfall with strong winds during monsoon.
food_scene: Buffet-style or set-menu dining in resorts with focus on seafood and Indian dishes.
local_culture: Islamic island communities with fishing and coconut-based livelihoods.
local_customs: Dress modestly away from resort beach zones; respect local religious norms.
festivals_events: Local religious and community festivals; island stays focus on nature rather than events.
unique_experiences: Highly restricted tropical islands where limited resorts and regulations keep beaches exceptionally quiet and ecologically intact.
best_seasons: November-March for calmer seas and best visibility.
avoid_seasons: South-west monsoon for rough seas and limited boat options; some services may halt.

road_connectivity: Access via NH66 and interior roads; promoted as part of Malanad Malabar Cruise and rural circuits tying rivers, backwaters and villages.
atm_availability: ATMs in nearby towns; cash still useful in small villages.
internet_connectivity: 4G in most villages near main roads; weaker in interior waterways.
peak_tourist_season: Winter months when circuits and cruises see more bookings.
off_season: Rains and off-peak months; good for very quiet, local-focused stays
rainfall_pattern: Heavy South West monsoon; region turns intensely green.
food_scene: Home-style Malabar and coastal Karnataka cuisine with rice, fish and coconut dominating.
local_culture: Blend of Kerala and coastal Karnataka traditions in food, dress and temple architecture.
local_customs: Observe temple dress codes and separate areas for non-Hindus where applicable.
festivals_events: Theyyam season in North Kerala and multiple temple festivals; rural circuit itineraries often overlap festival times.
unique_experiences: Less-commercialised backwater and rural zones compared to central Kerala, with combined Karnataka-Kerala culture.
best_seasons: November-March for comfortable temperatures and navigable water levels.
avoid_seasons: Peak monsoon floods and very humid shoulder weeks; boat schedules can change.

road_connectivity: Part of nationally promoted Krishna Circuit covering key sites in UP, Gujarat, Rajasthan, Haryana and Odisha; main nodes have strong highway and rail links.
atm_availability: Widely available in main circuit towns.
internet_connectivity: Good 4G in main towns; some ashrams emphasize low-tech stays.
nearest_airport_name: Multiple gateways (Delhi for Mathura-Vrindavan, Jamnagar/Rajkot for Dwarka)
peak_tourist_season: Janmashtami and major festival periods; long weekends and school vacations.
off_season: Non-festival weekdays outside winter
rainfall_pattern: Typical monsoon on plains and Saurashtra coast; some temples see crowds during Shravan/monsoon festivals.
food_scene: Predominantly vegetarian with many satvik and temple-linked eateries.
local_culture: Strong Vaishnav devotional traditions with daily rituals, bhajans and prasad offerings.
local_customs: Dress modestly, especially in temple interiors; remove footwear and follow queue systems.
festivals_events: Janmashtami, Holi in Braj region, Kartik and other key Vaishnav festivals draw large crowds.
unique_experiences: Multi-state circuit centred on the life and legends of Krishna, linking riverfront ghats, historic temples and coastal shrines.
activities_available: Heritage walks in old temple towns
accommodation_types: Some higher-end hotels in larger nodes
best_seasons: October-March for manageable temperatures on north and west Indian plains.
avoid_seasons: Hottest summer months for long queues and heat stress; monsoon for some travel disruptions.

road_connectivity: Excellent highway and bus connectivity from Delhi, Dehradun and other north Indian cities.
atm_availability: Ample ATMs in both towns.
internet_connectivity: Strong 4G and Wi-Fi in most ashrams, cafes and hotels.
peak_tourist_season: Festivals, long weekends and winter months; Char Dham season brings high pilgrim flows through Haridwar-Rishikesh.
off_season: Monsoon and very hot weeks before rains, except for serious sadhaks who stay year-round
rainfall_pattern: North Indian monsoon with occasional intense spells that raise Ganga levels.
food_scene: Predominantly vegetarian with many cafes serving Indian and continental health-focused dishes.
local_culture: Deeply religious Ganga-town culture with daily rituals, kirtans and satsangs.
local_customs: Dress modestly at ghats and temples; avoid photography during worship where restricted.
festivals_events: Kumbh (periodic in Haridwar), Kanwar Yatra, Ganga Dussehra and numerous ashram events.
unique_experiences: Gateway to the Himalayas where Ganga emerges from the hills, combining yoga, spiritual stays and soft adventure.
best_seasons: September-April for comfortable weather and active yoga/retreat calendar.
avoid_seasons: Peak monsoon for high river levels and landslides; high summer afternoons can be hot in Haridwar.

road_connectivity: Connected to major north Indian cities by highways and frequent trains; city traffic is dense in old quarters.
atm_availability: Numerous ATMs across city.
internet_connectivity: Good 4G in most parts of the city; some ghats have patchier coverage.
peak_tourist_season: Winter months, festivals like Dev Deepawali and Kartik Purnima; also popular during key Hindu festivals.
off_season: Mid-summer and parts of monsoon (excluding festival dates)
rainfall_pattern: Typical Ganga plain monsoon; high water can submerge lower ghat steps.
food_scene: Mostly vegetarian, with street food staples like kachori-sabzi, chaat and sweets, plus cafes in touristy pockets.
local_culture: Strongly devotional Hindu culture with continuous aartis, yagya and Sanskrit chanting traditions.
local_customs: Dress modestly; remove footwear at temples; avoid photography at cremation ghats unless explicitly allowed.
festivals_events: Dev Deepawali, Kartik month rituals, Holi (nearby), and countless local temple festivals.
unique_experiences: One of the world's oldest living cities, with continuous ritual life along the Ganga and dense historic lanes.
activities_available: Walking tours of lanes and ghats
best_seasons: October-March for more comfortable temperatures and clear river mornings.
avoid_seasons: Peak summer heat and humidity; some monsoon weeks with very high river levels.

road_connectivity: Connected by highways to Patna and neighbouring states; forms part of the broader Buddhist Circuit linking Sarnath, Kushinagar, Lumbini etc.
atm_availability: ATMs in town and nearby city of Gaya.
internet_connectivity: 4G in town; Wi-Fi in most guesthouses and cafes.
peak_tourist_season: Winter months, especially around major Buddhist festivals and teaching events.
off_season: Hot months with fewer foreign groups; useful for very quiet retreats
rainfall_pattern: Ganga plain monsoon with occasional heavy spells.
food_scene: Simple vegetarian and multi-cuisine cafes serving travellers and monastic communities.
local_culture: Mix of local Bihari communities with international Buddhist presence.
local_customs: Dress modestly and move clockwise (pradakshina) around sacred structures as per traditions.
festivals_events: Buddha Purnima and periodic large-scale teachings by senior monks and teachers.
unique_experiences: Site of Buddha's enlightenment, drawing monks, meditators and pilgrims from across the world.
activities_available: Visits to nearby Buddhist sites in the circuit
best_seasons: October-March for pleasant weather and active international pilgrimage season.
avoid_seasons: Peak summer heat; some monsoon periods for humidity and waterlogging.

road_connectivity: Linked to mainland via iconic Pamban Bridge; buses and cars connect from Madurai and other Tamil Nadu cities.
atm_availability: ATMs in town and on approach roads.
internet_connectivity: Functional 4G in town; patchy in some outlying coastal stretches.
peak_tourist_season: Festival periods, school vacations and long weekends; temple lines can be long.
off_season: Non-festival weekdays outside winter
rainfall_pattern: Influenced by both south-west and north-east monsoon, with heaviest spells in Oct-Dec.
food_scene: Vegetarian and coastal South Indian cuisine dominated by tiffin items and thalis.
local_culture: Devotional Shaivite town with strong temple economy and seafaring links.
local_customs: Maintain decorum during rituals; follow temple queues and instructions from priests.
festivals_events: Shivratri and other major Hindu festival days see big inflows.
unique_experiences: A coastal pilgrimage combining legendary Ramayana associations with a ritual walk through multiple sacred water points.
activities_available: Temple darshans and ritual baths at designated wells/ghats
Walks along sea and bridge viewpoints
Short drives to Dhanushkodi ruins and beaches
best_seasons: October-March for relatively milder heat and calmer seas.
avoid_seasons: Peak summer and days with active cyclonic systems in Bay of Bengal.

road_connectivity: Good highways connect Bengaluru, Goa and Hyderabad to Hosapete-Hampi; Pattadakal is accessed via Badami-Aihole road network.
atm_availability: ATMs in Hosapete and main villages.
internet_connectivity: 4G in Hosapete and most village cores; may weaken inside deeper ruin clusters.
peak_tourist_season: Winter holidays and long weekends; also around major local festivals.
off_season: Shoulder months and hotter weeks (for those tolerant of heat)
rainfall_pattern: Semi-arid with moderate monsoon; boulders and ruins dry quickly after showers.
food_scene: Simple South Indian, North Indian and traveller-oriented cafes near main bazaar zones.
local_culture: Rural Karnataka communities interwoven with heritage tourism economy.
local_customs: Avoid climbing on fragile structures; follow ASI guidelines at sites.
festivals_events: Hampi Utsav and other cultural events highlight music and dance against monument backdrops.
unique_experiences: Surreal boulder-strewn landscapes dotted with Vijayanagara capital ruins, combined with early temple experiments and Chalukyan art nearby.
activities_available: Day trips linking Hampi with Pattadakal-Badami-Aihole
best_seasons: October-March for bearable daytime heat and clearer skies.
avoid_seasons: Peak summer; some monsoon weeks when paths become slick among boulders.

road_connectivity: Hill road from Srinagar to Gulmarg; winter snow can impact driving time but route is popular and well-used.
atm_availability: Limited ATMs in/around Gulmarg; carry some cash from Srinagar.
internet_connectivity: Variable; main hotels usually offer Wi-Fi; mobile data quality depends on current J&K restrictions and networks.
peak_tourist_season: Winter school holidays and long weekends; also busy in summer for meadows and views.
off_season: Late spring and autumn shoulder periods with fewer visitors
rainfall_pattern: Snowfall dominates winter; shoulder months see rain/snow mix.
food_scene: Kashmiri and North Indian dishes with hearty winter meals in hotels and dhabas.
local_culture: Mountain communities with tourism and pastoral livelihoods; winter economy strongly ski-oriented.
local_customs: Negotiation for sleds/ponies is common; agree prices clearly beforehand.
festivals_events: Winter sports events and ski competitions occasionally organised.
unique_experiences: Global-level ski terrain with high-altitude powder slopes and a famous gondola, set within classic Kashmir scenery.
activities_available: Gondola rides for vistas and high-altitude access
best_seasons: December-March for snow sports, with peak conditions often Jan-Feb.
avoid_seasons: Shoulder weeks with slushy snow; heavy storm days when lifts may be closed.

road_connectivity: Mountain roads via Rishikesh-Joshimath; cable car and mountain roads connect Joshimath to Auli slopes.
atm_availability: ATMs mainly in Joshimath; carry cash to Auli.
internet_connectivity: Basic 4G/Wi-Fi around resorts and Joshimath; may be slow during bad weather.
peak_tourist_season: Winter holiday weeks and long weekends; also busy during specific snow-festival events.
off_season: Most of year outside snow window; summer sees some trekking traffic but no skiing
rainfall_pattern: Snow in winter, rain in shoulder/monsoon; road conditions can be impacted by weather.
food_scene: Hotel-based dining with North Indian and Garhwali dishes; limited independent cafes in peak snow belt.
local_culture: Garhwali hill communities; winter months bring seasonal tourism focus.
local_customs: Respect local temple norms in Joshimath and surrounding villages.
festivals_events: Occasional skiing championships and winter events.
unique_experiences: Well-structured, family-friendly ski slopes with spectacular Himalayan backdrops.
best_seasons: January-March for reliable snow on slopes and comfortable winter stays.
avoid_seasons: Weeks with patchy snowfall; monsoon when access roads can be affected.

road_connectivity: State highways connect from Chennai, Bengaluru and Puducherry; part of southern spiritual routes.
atm_availability: ATMs in town centre.
internet_connectivity: 4G in town; some ashrams intentionally keep Wi-Fi limited.
peak_tourist_season: Full-moon nights and Karthigai Deepam festival when massive crowds arrive.
off_season: Non-festival weekdays and off-moon days for quieter stays
rainfall_pattern: Receives north-east monsoon rains in Oct-Dec.
food_scene: Mostly vegetarian tiffin and thalis; ashram food is simple and sattvic.
local_culture: Strong Shaivite devotional culture with continuous worship and pilgrim movement.
local_customs: Dress modestly; many people walk girivalam barefoot as a vow.
festivals_events: Karthigai Deepam, full-moon girivalam days and numerous temple festivals.
unique_experiences: Fire-element associated hill considered a powerful spiritual centre for self-inquiry and meditation.
accommodation_types: Simple hotels and a few boutique stays
avoid_seasons: Hottest late-summer weeks for long barefoot walks; heavy-rain days.

road_connectivity: Hilly forest roads connect from Madhya Pradesh and Chhattisgarh; part of emerging nature-spiritual itineraries.
atm_availability: ATMs in nearby small towns; carry cash for local spending.
internet_connectivity: Limited; some 4G near town centre, weaker deeper into forest.
peak_tourist_season: Winter vacation weeks and certain festival dates.
off_season: Monsoon and hot months; suited only to those prepared for basic conditions
rainfall_pattern: Forest plateau monsoon; streams and waterfalls swell in rains.
food_scene: Basic vegetarian meals; limited restaurant variety.
local_culture: Central Indian hill communities with strong river-reverence traditions.
local_customs: Maintain silence and cleanliness at river-source spots regarded as highly sacred.
festivals_events: Local river festivals and religious gatherings at origin points.
unique_experiences: Jungle-edge plateau with river origins, mixing quiet nature with low-key spiritual sites.
activities_available: Short hikes to falls and forest viewpoints
best_seasons: October-March for cool, dry weather and walkable trails.
avoid_seasons: Heavy monsoon for leechy, slippery trails; very hot pre-monsoon months.

road_connectivity: Starting point for Char Dham and multiple Himalayan yatras; extensive bus and taxi networks operate in season.
atm_availability: Ample ATMs and banking services.
internet_connectivity: Good 4G; vital for coordination of hill logistics and weather checks.
peak_tourist_season: Char Dham peak months and major festivals like Kumbh years; spiritual travel trends cite strong demand.
off_season: Non-yatra monsoon stretch and some winter weeks, when hill shrines are closed
rainfall_pattern: Monsoon impacts onward routes more than base towns; still sees heavy showers.
food_scene: Vegetarian restaurants and langar/annadan setups for pilgrims.
local_culture: Highly devotional Ganga towns with strong yatra support ecosystem.
local_customs: Queue discipline and modest dress are expected; respect lane closures and police directions in festival time.
festivals_events: Kumbh (periodically), Kanwar Yatra and multiple fairs create intense surges.
unique_experiences: Serves as basecamp for some of India's most significant Himalayan pilgrimages while also offering stand-alone spiritual stays.
activities_available: Short local darshans and Ganga Aarti
Booking and orientation for hill pilgrimages
best_seasons: Char Dham window (roughly April/May-Oct, excluding heavy-rain weeks) plus separate Sep-Apr spiritual-stay season.
avoid_seasons: Peak monsoon for landslides in upper Garhwal; very hot May days for those not proceeding uphill.
